title: Five Words First
tag: One classroom move, under three minutes, for the teacher who teaches content, not English.

beats.say: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move one: five words first. Three minutes.

chunks.text: Six Moves, from EL Publishing. Move one: five words first. Three minutes.

beats.say: Here's the problem. A newcomer sits in your biology class. You start teaching photosynthesis. By the second sentence they're lost — not because they can't do science, but because four of the words in that sentence are new, and nobody said them first.

chunks.text: Here's the problem. A newcomer sits in your biology class. You start teaching photosynthesis.
By the second sentence they're lost — not because they can't do science, but because four of the words in that sentence are new, and nobody said them first.

beats.say: The usual fix is a vocabulary list. Thirty words on Monday, a quiz on Friday. The English learner learns none of them, because thirty words with no context is noise.

chunks.text: The usual fix is a vocabulary list. Thirty words on Monday, a quiz on Friday.
The English learner learns none of them, because thirty words with no context is noise.

beats.say: The move is smaller than that. Before the lesson, pick five words. Not twenty. Five. The ones that, if a student doesn't have them, the whole lesson falls apart.

chunks.text: The move is smaller than that. Before the lesson, pick five words. Not twenty. Five.
The ones that, if a student doesn't have them, the whole lesson falls apart.
For photosynthesis, that's probably sunlight.
Energy.
Carbon dioxide.
Oxygen.
And glucose.

beats.say: Put them on the board before you start. A picture or a symbol next to each one. Say each word. Have the whole class say it back. That's three minutes, and it's the best three minutes of the period.

chunks.text: Put them on the board before you start. A picture or a symbol next to each one. Say each word.
Have the whole class say it back. That's three minutes, and it's the best three minutes of the period.

beats.say: If your English learners speak Spanish, look at those five again. Four of them are cognates. Write the Spanish next to the English. You don't have to speak it. You just have to show the student that the big scary word is a word they already own.

a: Say the word · point to it
Use it ten times, the same way
Students say it in a pair
beats.say: Then, in the lesson, use the five words on purpose. Say the word and point to it on the board. Use the same word every time — if you said carbon dioxide at the start, don't switch to C O two ten minutes later without saying those are the same. Have students say the word to a partner. Put it on the exit ticket.

chunks.text: Then, in the lesson, use the five words on purpose. Say the word and point to it on the board.
Use the same word every time — if you said carbon dioxide at the start, don't switch to C O two ten minutes later without saying those are the same.
Have students say the word to a partner. Put it on the exit ticket.

beats.say: That's the whole move. Five words, a picture each, said out loud before the lesson, used ten times during it. Every level of English learner can get in the door of a lesson that starts this way — and so can the kid in the back who was never going to read the vocabulary list anyway.
